source.title: Really Strong Features Found in Residual Stream

record.tranche_reason: The post reports exploratory SAE-feature results in Pythia, not an audit of model neurons or neuron poles, and does not test any listed version's claim.
record.gate_note: The post reports ablations of residual-stream SAE feature directions and their effects. These are not measurements of the model's own neurons, attribution graphs, or held-out prediction scores, so the results do not test the listed versions. No values cited from other work are recorded as results.
record.test_reason: An early informal post training a sparse autoencoder on Pythia-70M layer-2 residual-stream activations and showing a few hand-picked features with logit lens and token ablations. It audits no model neurons or neuron poles, reports no shares of interpretable units, builds no attribution graphs, and does no held-out or simulation scoring. So no version is tested. The SAE features are a different construct from the model's own neurons, which the claim is about.
record.authors_conclusion: Roughly correct. The author says the residual-stream SAE features are strong and intuitive, unlike the earlier MLP-layer features. He frames the decomposition as promising, with low reconstruction loss and a usable way to specify traits. He also says due diligence, baseline comparisons and hyperparameter search remain to be done.
record.recipe_differences: The post trains an overcomplete sparse autoencoder on layer-2 residual-stream activations and inspects feature directions with examples, logit lens, and token ablations. It does not audit model neuron poles or report the claimed shares.

fits_no_version.finding: An overcomplete SAE on Pythia-70M layer-2 residual stream yields 3k+ features, mostly single or combined words. A few hand-picked features (Stack Exchange, Title Case, Last Name, [word] and [word]) show intuitive ablation and logit-lens effects.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Dictionary-learned residual-stream features in small LMs are often interpretable and causally affect predictions when ablated.

record.problems: The author describes the work as preliminary and says due diligence, baseline comparisons, and normal hyperparameter search remain. Several feature interpretations are tentative, and the author says some effects were not rigorously studied. No quantitative feature-share estimates or uncertainty measures are reported.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result relevant to the claim was left out.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit and no shares.
No cross-model shares of interpretable neurons.
No InceptionV1 or canonical polysemantic neuron analysis.
No comparison of tools or architectures for neuron interpretability.
No test of explanations' predictions on held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal preliminary LessWrong/Alignment Forum post with no quantitative shares. Its stance favours dictionary learning over raw neurons, which loosely sits opposite the essay's thesis but does not test it. The model naming is ambiguous (the author says '70m (actually named 160M!)').

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, neuron-pole counts, or shares of poles by number of jobs or understanding.
No cross-model comparison or estimates of the claimed shares across model sizes or architectures.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neuron or test of the proposed shared-pose explanation.
No comparison of architecture, regularization, or tools, and no estimate of interpretability shares in vision models.
No attribution graphs or test of whether model neurons suffice to explain behavior without a replacement model.
No test of whether explanations written from activating examples predict firing on separate examples.
No automated scoring of explanations by simulating activations on new text.

tranche.reason: Informal SAE feature showcase on the Pythia-70M layer-2 residual stream. It audits no model neurons and reports no shares of interpretable units, so it bears on no version.

source_check.notes: All rows are SAE feature results (Pythia-70M, which the author says is named 160M; layer 2 resid_post), not neuron results. They are qualitative and have no baselines. In the comments, StefanHex uses 'neuron' for SAE hidden units, which could be misread. The ~50% Last Name figure comes from an informal comment. r1's 'High Level Picture' locator is slightly off: the 'majority single word' sentence is in the opening paragraph.
